newsitem.title: UK: Crude oil tanker rates mostly flat to weak.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil tanker rates mostly flat to weak.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were mostly steady to weak on Friday and earlier signs of interest for transatlantic business appeared to have fizzled out, shipping brokers said.

"The North Sea has been quiet," one broker said. He assessed rates for Aframaxes crossing the Atlantic at around W107.5 for U.S. Gulf destinations, and very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were talked at around W60.
While one brokerage reported the fixture of the 83,000 tonne Torinita from Nigg Bay to the U.S Gulf at W107.5, others doubted the fixture and said they thought the ship still available.
West African tankering appeared to pick up after a few days' relative inactivity, with three VLCCs fixed eastwards at around W53, and one fixed to the U.S. Gulf at W60.

Rates for million-barrel ships for the latter route were assessed unchanged at W90 for older vessels and at W95 for the newer ships. The 130,000 tonne Corcovado was fixed from Escravos to the U.S. Gulf at W90.
Caribbean markets were again becalmed and 70,000 tonne ships were assessed at W130-135, with the 70,000 tonne Bona Ranger fixed at the upper end of this range.
"It has been stuck in this range for a while," one broker said. "There are a few ships around over there so things could come off."

Middle eastern markets were less active, following Tokyo Tankers's fixture on Thursday of the modern 275,000 tonne Golar Edinburgh at W62.5 to Japan. A fixture was made on Friday of the 250,000 tonne Torino to Taiwan at W56.
Brokers assessed the Mideast-U.S. market at around W55 for VLCCs, while UK/Med options were worth a couple of points more.
